correctness.rationale: For any period-p repetition in a three-one word, the repeated primitive length-p block contains exactly one one. Hence every one-containing run corresponds to one of the two adjacent one distances; the flank sums and equal-gap merger give a complete formula. Splitting b=c and b≠c proves the exact rational GF, while the extremal GF and standard coefficient estimates prove the sharp threshold and limiting half-half law. An independent brute least-period interval check passed all 8855 words through length 22, and bivariate coefficient checks passed through length 36. These are checks, not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Actual searches of published mathematical records, OEIS-style tables and primary full texts found no fixed-three-one maximal-periodic-run gap classification, complete bivariate run-count spectrum or fair-coin limit. The closest classical theorems concern unconditioned bounds, algorithms or summed run lengths, not this conditional count. Possible unindexed equivalent work remains a priority risk.
residual_risks: Historical priority cannot be guaranteed from search, especially if an equivalent fixed-weight specialization is described only within an unindexed appendix or textbook.
The word “runs” is ambiguous: ordinary symbol runs and maximal periodicity runs must not be conflated.
A future broader exact fixed-composition theorem might subsume this result; none was found in accessible sources.

value.rationale: A full structural classification of maximal periodicities under a natural sparse-content restriction identifies all possible interacting periods and their sharp six-run boundary. The result supplies an exact all-length bivariate distribution and a nontrivial half-half probabilistic limit. These are natural invariants and infinite-family statements, not a small table increment or mechanical substitution into existing unrestricted run bounds.
